Adora Magic City Review

Review of Adora Magic City

The 2023-built/2024-inaugurated Adora Magic City cruise ship (also known as AIDA Modu) is the first of two China-built vessels ordered by CSSC CARNIVAL CRUISE and operated under the new travel brand Adora Cruises (2022-established and 2023-inaugurated).

Magic City's sister ship, Flora City, is scheduled for inauguration in 2026 Q4.

According to the shipbuilding contract, in addition to the two initial units (each costing US$ 770M/EUR 700M based on 2019 currency rates), there is an option for four more ships of the same class to be produced by SWS/Shanghai Waigaoqiao Shipbuilding Co. Ltd. The negotiated shipbuilding cost was reportedly about 1/5th cheaper than if the units were constructed in Europe.

The Adora Magic City vessel (IMO number 9871036) is currently Panama-flagged (MMSI 352001180) and registered in Colon. It is expected that, following the official delivery, the ship's registry/flag state will be changed to Hong Kong, China.

Adora Magic City (also known as Aida Modu/阿依达魔都) is the first large cruise ship manufactured in China, named in recognition of Shanghai’s local nickname, "Magic City" (魔法城). There are currently four mega-cities associated with this title: London (England), Tokyo (Japan), New York City (USA), and Shanghai (China).

History - construction and ownership

Adora Cruises Ltd (shipowner) is a joint venture company founded in October 2015 (originally as "CSSC Carnival Cruise Shipping Ltd" and renamed in June 2023). The company operates the fully owned subsidiary and travel brand, Adora Cruises. CSSC Carnival China was initially scheduled to begin operations in 2020, but due to the COVID-19 crisis, the brand's debut was postponed until 2023.

In January 2026, Astro Ocean International Cruise and Adora Cruises merged into the new travel brand China Cruises.

Adora Cruises' two newbuilds – Adora Magic City and Adora Flora City (2026) – are based on a modified Carnival VISTA design, represented by the sister ships Carnival Vista (2016), Carnival Horizon (2018), Carnival Panorama (2019), Carnival Venezia (2019-built as Costa Venezia), and Carnival Firenze (2020-built as Costa Firenze).

In comparison to the original Carnival VISTA design, the CSSC Adora ships have a Gross Tonnage of 136,200 GT (vs 133,596), Deadweight Tonnage (DWT) of 13,820 tons (vs 13,415), the same waterline beam (37 m/max width 46 m, with the Navigation Bridge’s wings), and the same draught (8.55 m/28 ft).

The vessel is equipped with a total of 20 lifeboats, each with a capacity of 314 seats.

 

For major construction milestones and events, visit the ship's Wiki page.

Decks and Cabins

Adora Magic City offers 2,125 staterooms, all of which include standard amenities such as 2 twin beds (convertible to Queen-size), a wardrobe, an electronic safe box, lifejackets (in the closet), a seating/lounge area (with mirrored vanity/writing desk and chair), a smart HDTV (with satellite reception and infotainment system), direct-dial phone, hairdryer, minibar, and an en-suite bathroom (WC, shower, mirrored single-sink vanity).

All balcony staterooms feature sofabeds to accommodate a 3rd or 4th passenger. WiFi is available in all staterooms for an additional charge, as well as in public areas. Suites receive free 24-hour room service, slippers, bathrobes, a drinks package, and a personal valet.

The ship has 16 decks, 14 of which are passenger-accessible, and 12 contain cabins.

The ship also has a total of 701 crew cabins, with a capacity to accommodate 1,292 staff/crew members.

Shipboard facilities and amenities

Confirmed amenities onboard include a large performing arts center, numerous restaurants and cafes (both complimentary and specialty dining venues), various lounges and bars, art corridors, children's clubs, a spa, an outdoor amusement park with a circular-shaped waterslide, and a kids' playground with 11 water-play features. A spacious sunbathing area is available for children.

The 16-story ship offers an expansive 40,000 m² (430,556 ft²) of public space.

The Aquapark features three water slides spanning four decks. Additional fun facilities include the Rope Garden (an outdoor activity course with 360-degree sea views) and the VR/Virtual Reality gaming center.

The ship has a total of 16x elevators (passenger lifts) positioned forward (8), midship (4) and aft (4).

The next review is based on the sistership Carnival Venezia, which was thoroughly redesigned during an extensive drydock in 2023 following its transfer from Costa to CCL-Carnival Cruise Line.

Adora Magic City has a complimentary Main Dining Room (on two levels/decks 4-5, waiter-served) open for Breakfast, Brunch (seadays only), Lunch (seadays only), and Dinner. On port days, breakfast is served between 7:30-9:30 am (closed for lunch). Dining room hours are subject to change based on the itinerary/port arrival times or scheduled onboard activities. On seadays, one MDR serves Brunch (breakfast and lunch between 8:30 am - 1 pm), while the other MDR serves Breakfast (between 8-10 am) and Lunch (between 12-noon and 1:30 pm). Afternoon Tea service (between 3-4 pm/seadays only) is complimentary and includes a selection of teas, paninis/mini sandwiches, and sweets. Dinner (seadays/portdays) is served with 2 fixed/pre-assigned seatings - Early (at 6 pm) and Late (at 8:15 pm), plus Anytime ("Your Time Dining" between 5:45-9:30 pm).

The Lido Restaurant is also complimentary and operates as a self-service buffet restaurant offering open-seating Breakfast (7:30 am - 12 noon, made-to-order omelet station), Lunch (12-noon - 2:30 pm), Dinner (6-9:30 pm, Good Eats buffet), and Late Night Snacks (11 pm - 1 am). The Good Eats buffet menu is an alternative to the Main Dining Room, offering steaks, prime rib, grilled chicken, pastas, salads, desserts, and a daily Chef's Special. The Lido Restaurant features various take-away food stations and themed food bars, including Adora Deli (sandwiches, draught beer dispenser), Mongolian Wok (stir-fry, made-to-order Asian food), Pasta Bar (choice of pastas, sauces, toppings), Salad Bar (35 items), Pizza Bar (24-hour Pizzeria), Chef's Choice Bar (international cuisine), Hot and Cold Buffet (stir-fries, pasta, carving station), Grille (burgers, hot dogs, fries, chicken sandwiches), and a Dessert Bar (also offering sugar-free items). The Lido Buffet also includes a 24-hour self-serve tea/coffee station and machines for soft ice cream and yogurt.

As is typical for Carnival ships, Adora Magic City offers signature dining venues such as:

  • Seafood Restaurant (lunch and dinner, waiter service), with indoor/outdoor seating, à la carte menu, offering lobster, shrimp, crab cakes, oysters, Fish & Chips, and other specialties.
  • Steakhouse (at a surcharge, reservations recommended), serving appetizers, salads, steaks (prime-aged beef), ribeye, filet mignon, lamb chops, lobster, fish, and desserts. The food is wheeled to the table for examination, and a cooking demonstration is offered.
  • Teppanyaki Sushi Restaurant (reservations required), serving Far East specialties with a live cooking performance at custom-built cooking stations.
  • Pizzeria (complimentary, 24-hour, self-serve) offering fresh-baked pizzas and made-to-order pies.
  • BBQ Restaurant (outdoor bar open on seadays only) offering fast food grilled items such as steak, pork, chicken, sliders, and BBQ tacos.

The ship's main show lounge, Metropol Theater (capacity 975 seats), hosts grand-style productions with live performances (tribute acts, singing, and dancing), combined with sound and lighting special effects. Evening shows last 30 minutes, and music is supported by HD media projected on large LED screens. During the day, the Theater hosts seminars, lectures, multimedia presentations, bingo, port talks, and other enrichment activities.

China's first Comedy Theater at Sea is a partnership with Mahua FunAge (Kaixin Mahua Cultural Tourism Development Co. Ltd.).

The ship also has a complimentary outdoor Cinema with a large LED screen, showing funny videos, TV shows, concerts, live sporting events, and evening movies (under the stars) with complimentary popcorn.

Adora Magic City features a large Casino (with Annex/VIP Room) offering slot machines and table games like Craps, Roulette, and Black Jack. The casino is closed when the ship is in port and opens 30-60 minutes after departure.

Other notable features include the large Adora Shopping Center/Plaza (duty-free mall with luxury-brand boutiques), Photo Gallery & Shop, Art Gallery, Wellness Complex, and outdoor activities like SkyCourse (suspended ropes course), Multi-Sports Course, and Mini-Golf Course.

Itineraries

Adora Magic City's itinerary program is based on homeporting in Shanghai, China, offering roundtrip voyages targeting Chinese/East Asian tourists. The Maiden Voyage (from Shanghai Wusongkou Terminal) was initially scheduled for December 21, 2023, and later postponed to January 1, 2024.

Bookings for the inaugural cruise opened on September 20, 2023.

The original 6-night/7-day maiden sailing was a roundtrip from Shenzhen/Shekou to Japan, visiting Miyako/Iwate (day 3) and Naha/Okinawa (day 5). Prices started from NT$34,405 (~US$1,060) per person, including taxes.

A 4-day test voyage was conducted from December 25-29, with the liner staying overnight in Kagoshima, Japan (Dec 26-27).

Adora Magic City's inaugural cruise (first commercial voyage) departed from Shanghai Wusongkou on January 1st, visiting Seogwipo (Jeju Island, South Korea), Nagasaki, and Fukuoka in Japan.

Adora Magic City is based in Asia year-round, offering roundtrips from Shenzhen, Shanghai and other Chinese homeports.

Adora’s fleet operates year-round in Asia, with 7-day and longer itineraries combining domestic routes with popular destinations in Japan, Korea, and some Southeast Asian countries.

Adora Magic City Wiki

The vessel (SWS Shanghai Waigaoqiao yard/hull number H1508) has a gross tonnage of 136,201 GT, a deadweight tonnage (DWT) of 13,820 tons, and a maximum draught of 8.6 meters. Its powerplant consists of five MAN marine diesel engines (4-stroke, common-rail injection: 2x 14V48/60CR plus 3x 8L48/60CR) with a combined output of 62.4 MW (83,680 hp). The propulsion system is diesel-electric, featuring two ABB Azipod thrusters with a combined output of 33 MW (44,250 hp). The registered shipowner and manager is CSSC CARNIVAL CRUISE SHIPPING Ltd, based in Hong Kong.

The shipbuilding contract between CSSC (China State Shipbuilding Corporation, parent of Shanghai Waigaoqiao Shipbuilding Co. Ltd.) and Carnival Corporation plc was signed in February 2017. Between 2017 and 2019, the shipyard invested approximately USD 260 million in upgrades to accommodate the construction of China’s largest passenger ships.

The contract for the vessel's design (CCL VISTA modified) and construction was signed on November 6, 2018, during the "China International Import Expo 2018." The shipbuilding order was for 2+4 units (two ordered plus four optional).

The vessel's construction officially began on October 17, 2019, with the steel-cutting ceremony held at the SWS-Shanghai Waigaoqiao Shipbuilding yard in Shanghai, China.

The physical construction/assembly started with the keel-laying/coin ceremony on November 10, 2020, at SWS. The special event was attended by Michele Cecchi (Italy's Consul General in Shanghai), Wu Qing (Shanghai's Deputy Mayor), Lei Fanpei (CSSC's Chairman), Giuseppe Bono (Fincantieri Group's CEO), Fabrizio Ferri (Fincantieri China's CEO), Tian Yulong (MIIT's Chief Engineer), and Gao Dongsheng (MIIT's General Manager). MIIT stands for China's "Ministry of Industry and Information Technology."

The hull and superstructure were completed (in drydock) on November 2, 2021.

The vessel (yard/hull number H1508) was launched/floated out from drydock on December 17, 2021. The drydock's flooding began on December 16, and, following tradition in China, the ship's bow was decorated with banners. The launch ceremony featured water spraying on the bow, creating a rainbow. On launch day, the vessel was reported to be 55% complete. After floating, it was moored at a dock for interior outfitting. The launch event was addressed via live stream by Arnold Donald (Carnival Corporation's CEO).

The ship's first main engine/diesel generator was started for the first time on July 26, 2022.

The design was redeveloped by CSSC, with some technologies and consulting provided by the Italian shipbuilder Fincantieri. The design incorporates approximately 25 million different components and parts, 107 systems, 55,000 equipment sets, 4,180 km/2,600+ miles of cabling, 365 km/227 miles of pipelines, and 120 km/75 miles of air pipes. The construction work involved about 12 million man-hours, 5,000+ engineers and technicians (from 32 countries), 361 suppliers (domestic and foreign), and 1,105 businesses/companies.

Being the owner of the patented Carnival VISTA-class platform, Fincantieri set up a joint venture with CCTD (Fincantieri China Ltd) to grant the technology license for the vessel platform and to provide technical services to the shipbuilder (SWS), including project and supply chain management, and sales of the ship's main systems and components. Fincantieri’s subsidiary Marine Interiors was contracted to design, prefabricate, and install the ship's public areas, catering facilities, all glass walls, and all cabins (passenger + crew/~2,800 units).

The powerplant is based on one main diesel generator (model Wartsila 31, 9.6 MW) with a total power output of 62.4 MW. The propulsion system uses two ABB Azipods (steerable/360-degree rotating pod propellers powered by electric motors) with a power output of 16.8 MW. The ship's maximum speed is 22.6 knots.

In late March 2019, SWS contracted ABB Ltd (1988-founded, Zurich, Switzerland-based manufacturer of marine propulsion and robotics/automation systems) to supply and install the ship's Azipods. The contract was signed by Gang Chen (Shanghai Waigaoqiao Shipbuilding's General Manager) and Peter Terwiesch (ABB Industrial Automation's President). The ABB package also includes the entire electric powerplant (electricity generators, main switchboards, transformers). The propulsion control for the Azipods (from the Navigation Bridge) includes remote diagnostics provided by ABB Ability Collaborative Centers (land-based facilities for real-time data gathering and analysis).

The cruise ship is equipped with shore-power connectivity. This technology allows the main diesel engines to be shut down while berthed, reducing in-port noise and pollution (COx and NOx emissions and soot particles). While moored, the ship uses the port city's electrical grid to supply power for all onboard facilities and services.

On December 12, 2022, Adora Cruises signed a strategic partnership with China Duty-Free Cruise Services Ltd (2018-founded subsidiary of CDFG/China Duty-Free Group Co. Ltd.) for the management of the ship's duty-free shopping center. CDFG is a state-owned retailer and China's only company authorized to provide duty-free services (business, offshore, overseas, and other).

In February 2023, SWS reported that the ship was 87% complete.

In April 2023, assembly began on the ship's amusement park, which includes a waterslide with a 5-meter/16-foot-high circular-shaped bowl slide (diameter 8 meters/26 feet).

The ship's name, Adora Magic City, was officially announced on May 19, 2023, by Chen Ranfeng (CSSC Carnival Cruise Shipping's Managing Director). The announcement took place at a special event in Shanghai, organized by the "Shanghai Municipal Administration of Culture and Tourism" and CCTD (CSSC Cruise Technology Development Co. Ltd.).

On June 1, 2023, the vessel was refloated in preparation for its official launch from the drydock, which occurred on June 7. The previous launch from the drydock (on December 17, 2021) was when the hull was floated temporarily.

The first set of sea trials was completed in July, and the second set was completed in September 2023.

Adora Magic City was officially delivered and named in Shanghai on November 4, 2023. The christening ceremony was held at Waigaoqiao Shipyard and led by godmother Fan Jinshi (1938-born Chinese archaeologist). The naming event was attended by government officials, representatives from CSSC (including Wen Gang/Chairman), Adora Cruises, major travel agencies, and media.

On June 6th, 2026, Adora Magic City left Shanghai Port, inaugurating China's first cruise-to-nowhere (portless) itinerary.
